summary:
We developed Earth System Trend Detective, an interactive 3D web-based climate investigation platform built with Three.js, Globe.gl, Leaflet.js, Chart.js, and Satellite.js. Starting from a real-time orbital command center tracking NASA Earth observation satellites, users dive through volumetric clouds into high-resolution satellite imagery across a four-tier hierarchy—spanning over 90 countries down to detailed local case studies in Kottayam and Kanjirappally, Kerala (India).

The project directly addresses the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge by transforming 20 years (2006–2025) of environmental metrics from NASA MODIS, GPM, GLDAS, Landsat, and ECOSTRESS datasets into an accessible analytical tool. Using an interactive timeline and on-the-fly statistical analysis—including linear regression slopes and Pearson correlation coefficients—users can evaluate significant links between rising surface temperatures, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, vegetation health (NDVI), and extreme monsoon cloudbursts such as the 2018 Kerala floods.

This work is important because turning complex satellite data into clear, localized evidence empowers communities, researchers, and policymakers to recognize climate shifts early and strengthen regional resilience.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive, 3D space-to-ground climate investigation platform built to turn users into Earth system detectives analyzing 20 years (2006–2025) of environmental change.

  • Phase 1 — Orbital Command Center: Users begin in space around a 3D Earth with J2000.0 celestial ephemeris lighting, a dense starfield, and real-time SGP4 orbital propagation tracking 8 NASA/Earth-observation platforms (Terra, Aqua, GPM Core, SMAP, Landsat 9, Suomi NPP, ICESat-2, and ISS/ECOSTRESS) using NORAD Two-Line Elements (TLEs). Users can inspect live satellite telemetry (sub-point coordinates, altitude, velocity) or click any country on the globe.
  • Cinematic Cloud-Dive Transition: Selecting a study area triggers a procedural Fractal Brownian Motion (FBM) volumetric cloud fly-through, seamlessly transitioning from orbital altitude down to high-resolution hybrid satellite imagery.
  • Phase 2 & 3 — Four-Tier Climate & Statistical Investigation: Using a synchronized Leaflet satellite map (with a toggleable 3D perspective tilt) and a glassmorphic analytics dashboard, users explore a Country → State/Province → District → Town hierarchy spanning 90+ countries worldwide, alongside a deep-dive case study into Kottayam and Kanjirappally, Kerala (India). An interactive 20-year bar timeline, sparkline cards, dual-mode charts (Temperature vs. Soil Moisture and Rainfall vs. NDVI), and an on-the-fly statistical engine calculate linear regression slopes and Pearson correlation coefficients (
    )across indicators derived from MODIS, GPM, GLDAS, SMAP, Landsat 8/9, ECOSTRESS, and GRACE-FO datasets.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Making Satellite Science Intuitive: Bridges the gap between complex orbital telemetry and everyday understanding by showing which NASA satellites observe the planet and what their long-term measurements reveal on the ground.
  • Actionable Local Context: Connects macro-scale climate shifts (such as regional warming and altered evapotranspiration) to hyper-local impacts—like extreme monsoon cloudbursts, the 2018 Kerala floods, soil moisture depletion, and urban heat islands.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Engineered as a portable, zero-install web application that runs directly in any modern browser, making it immediately usable by students, educators, citizen scientists, researchers, and local resilience planners.
  • Intended Impact: Empower communities and decision-makers—especially in climate-vulnerable regions like the Western Ghats—to recognize statistically significant environmental trends early and plan better flood mitigation, watershed management, and agricultural adaptation.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages & Core Web Tech: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (single-file architecture), HTML5 Canvas (procedural FBM cloud rendering).
  • 3D, Mapping & Data Visualization Libraries: Three.js (0.160.0), Globe.gl (2.30.0), Leaflet.js (1.9.4) with Esri World Imagery and Google Hybrid tiles, Chart.js (4.4.1), and Tailwind CSS.
  • Astrodynamics & Scientific Computing: Satellite.js (5.0.0) for SGP4 orbital propagation, J2000.0 ephemeris calculations, NORAD TLEs, and custom JavaScript linear regression / Pearson correlation functions.
  • NASA Data Sources & Missions Referenced: MODIS (Terra/Aqua), GPM IMERG, GLDAS, SMAP, Landsat 8/9, ECOSTRESS, VIIRS (Suomi NPP), ICESat-2, and GRACE-FO.
  • Development Environment & AI: Git, GitHub Pages for live deployment, standard consumer laptops/modern web browsers, and Generative AI (Gemini) used transparently as a pair-programming assistant for ephemeris math, volumetric cloud shaders/rendering, and visualization scaffolding.

How Is the Project Creative?

Rather than presenting climate data in static 2D tables or isolated graphs, our team designed a unified "mission control to street-level" narrative. Starting at live orbital mechanics, diving physically through sunlit procedural cloud decks, and landing on a tiltable 3D satellite map creates an emotional and spatial connection between global Earth observation and local lived reality. Combining real-time satellite tracking with a 4-level geographic drill-down and live statistical trend proof transforms passive data viewing into active scientific detective work.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  1. Accessibility & Portability: We intentionally built a lightweight, dependency-free single-file web architecture using pinned CDNs so anyone with a browser can launch it without servers, API keys, or local installations.
  2. Scientific Rigor Over Raw Visuals: We paired visual timelines with live linear regression slopes and Pearson correlation coefficients so users can distinguish normal year-to-year weather variability from statistically significant multi-decade climate shifts.
  3. Global Breadth + Local Depth: While supporting 90+ countries so users anywhere in the world can investigate their own region, we curated granular district- and town-level profiles for Kerala to demonstrate how regional climate forcing translates into localized flood and drought hazards.
  4. Usability & Interaction Polish: We carefully handled pointer-event layering over the 3D globe, added searchable breadcrumbs across all four geographic tiers, and ensured smooth transitions between orbital and surface views.
  5. Open Science & Transparency: In accordance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, we clearly documented all satellite mission inspirations and transparently disclosed AI-assisted development components.
